excluded.success: No transaction, durability or memory-safety claim is made for this alternative API.
excluded.failure: No success/error contract is claimed by P0 for this explicitly excluded family.
excluded.limitations: Source/API changes are still detected so the exclusion cannot silently expand.

value-accessor.preconditions: Valid receiver and any lifetime/ownership prerequisites of its containing type.
value-accessor.success: Returns the named stored field, view, mode, count, reference or diagnostic snapshot without a logical transaction commit.
value-accessor.failure: No returned error unless the signature returns Result/Option; such forms expose invalid storage or absent optional values. Allocation/panic and concurrent diagnostic consistency are not transactional outcomes.
value-accessor.limitations: Counters and independent reads are observations, not an atomic database snapshot.

table-new.preconditions: Exclusive creation in a valid arena; row_capacity fits available resources.
table-new.success: Allocates a new shared table header and empty physical slots; returns an unbound local handle.
table-new.failure: Allocation errors are returned; earlier bootstrap allocations need not be rolled back. Rust allocation panic/abort is separate.
table-new.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

table-attach.preconditions: Offsets originate from this exact arena/layout/type and identify initialized, live, unique table storage; attach only under the lifecycle contract.
table-attach.success: Builds a local handle after header-format and pointer checks; caller must bind every registered index.
table-attach.failure: InvalidPointer on failed checks; no logical publication.
table-attach.limitations: Bounds/format checks do not prove provenance, initialization or exclusive authority.

bind-index.preconditions: Quiescent bootstrap for first registration; same arena handle, correct initial postings and identical pure extractor across attachments.
bind-index.success: Registers index once, validates initial row/posting relation, binds shared owner and local extractor; later ordinary commits maintain it.
bind-index.failure: Index, incomplete/storage, registration-closed and capacity errors reject binding. Shared owner/registry preparation is not promised transactionally reversible on every exceptional path.
bind-index.limitations: Extractor identity/purity and bootstrap exclusion are caller obligations; callbacks must not reenter locked table/index operations.

begin.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects.
begin.success: Seals index registry, registers a fresh transaction, captures retained snapshot and creates empty local dependency/write sets.
begin.failure: Incomplete/mismatched/poisoned index state, pointer or ProcArray exhaustion/stale-registration errors return failure. Snapshot failure attempts deregistration; registration ownership and no-wrap remain boundaries.
begin.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

read.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects.
read.success: Returns latest pending value for that row, otherwise snapshot-visible value and records its version dependency; absent visible row returns None.
read.failure: Closed/wrong-table, binding/poison, out-of-range, pointer or foreign-row-lock/chain-limit SerializationFailure; earlier dependencies may remain. Caller aborts on failure, and commits before trusting returned observations.
read.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

index-read.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Requested index is bound; key representation/callback matches its registered semantics.
index-read.success: Returns sorted unique matching row IDs for snapshot plus own writes and records even empty predicate dependencies; stamps/candidates captured under predicate guards, values materialized after release.
index-read.failure: SerializationFailure if contention, too-new or changed stamp or foreign row lock; invalid binding/key/storage errors propagate. Dependencies may accumulate before failure; caller aborts.
index-read.limitations: Completeness is a target contract; native general-history refinement is not supplied by this inventory.

write.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Existing visible physical slot; T has the byte-representation prerequisites of coarse_dirty_mask_for_copy.
write.success: Allocates a private new version, retains original base and appends pending write; repeated writes select the final value at commit.
write.failure: Out-of-bounds/missing, conflict, pointer, allocation and transaction admission errors. No committed value changes; earlier private writes remain for abort/rollback.
write.limitations: No automatic physical insert; raw-byte padding validity is an explicit unresolved implementation/API enforcement issue.

write-mask.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Existing visible physical slot; supplied dirty mask is consistent with the selected WAL codec and changed fields.
write-mask.success: Appends private version with caller-supplied mask and original base; final write wins within the transaction.
write-mask.failure: Same admission, missing-row, conflict, pointer and allocation errors as write; no committed row publication.
write-mask.limitations: Caller mask correctness is not established by the public signature.

savepoint.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects.
savepoint.success: Appends a named write-set length; duplicate names are allowed and rollback chooses the latest.
savepoint.failure: Transaction admission errors; allocation panic/abort remains outside returned Result.
savepoint.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

rollback.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects.
rollback.success: Recycles writes after the latest matching savepoint; truncates later savepoints; retained read/predicate dependencies may conservatively force retry.
rollback.failure: SavepointNotFound or admission/storage cleanup error. Cleanup errors may occur after partial private recycling; never assume a clean reusable transaction after error.
rollback.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

abort.preconditions: Transaction created by this table/mapping; do not concurrently use/copy its registration.
abort.success: Recycles private writes, clears local sets and deregisters; already finished registration is harmless.
abort.failure: TransactionTableMismatch or cleanup/ProcArray error. A cleanup error can prevent later cleanup/deregistration; callers must handle failure as storage/lifecycle failure, not a committed transaction.
abort.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

commit.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Unlogged writes allowed only before WAL stream binding.
commit.success: Validates row, write-base and predicate dependencies; publishes final rows and index changes, deregisters, stamps, releases guards. Returns count or exact committed-write record; read-only commit returns zero writes.
commit.failure: SerializationFailure denotes rejected validation/acquisition and attempts abort cleanup. WalRequired rejects unlogged writes. Other admission/preparation errors may leave private state needing abort. Errors after source removal/publication or failed cleanup poison storage and are not clean aborts; exclusive recovery is required.
commit.limitations: Error enum alone does not encode every phase; failure classification and poison state matter. Arbitrary-history and exceptional cleanup implementation proofs remain open.

indexed-row-lock.preconditions: Acquire the entire sorted unique row set in one call before beginning the transaction; never extend the set while retaining another guard.
indexed-row-lock.success: Returns stable-slot coordination guards held until Drop; bounded try form returns SerializationFailure on contention and drops partial acquisitions.
indexed-row-lock.failure: Out-of-range/pointer errors; bounded try fails on exhausted attempts. Blocking form may wait indefinitely.
indexed-row-lock.limitations: Optional caller coordination, not predicate isolation or an automatically acquired database lock.

row-owner-lock.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Do not outlive the table/arena; obey owner guard lifetime.
row-owner-lock.success: Temporarily acquires partition guard, claims visible version owner flag and returns RowLockGuard; nested same-transaction claims do not clear outer ownership on Drop.
row-owner-lock.limitations: Returned owner flag is not a retained partition mutex; vacuum must preserve flagged nodes until guard Drop.

seed.preconditions: Exclusive bootstrap; no bound indexes/WAL stream; initialized matching payload representation.
seed.success: Allocates and publishes a version only in an empty physical slot.
seed.failure: Out-of-range, invalid storage, allocation, WalRequired, bound-index rejection or RowAlreadyExists. Failed head CAS can consume a private allocation; no rollback guarantee on bootstrap resources.
seed.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

recovery-write.preconditions: Exclusive recovery before binding indexes/WAL; valid row layout and replay input.
recovery-write.success: Installs recovered value with specified transaction ID; CAS variant replaces only expected head and reports false on mismatch.
recovery-write.failure: Bounds/storage/allocation/unmanaged-write errors; CAS mismatch returns false. Failed attempt can consume bootstrap allocation.
recovery-write.limitations: Recovery batches need not roll back an earlier applied prefix on error; discard/recover exclusively before serving.

latest.preconditions: Valid retained table/arena; diagnostic or exclusive bootstrap use; not a transactional read.
latest.success: Returns present physical head value or offset; snapshot_latest_rows holds all partitions while copying latest heads.
latest.failure: Out-of-range or invalid-pointer/binding errors according to entry point.
latest.limitations: latest_value and row_head_offset do not register snapshot dependencies or pin a returned pointer for later dereference.

clock-floor.preconditions: Exclusive recovery/bootstrap; requested floor obeys reserved-zero/no-wrap policy.
clock-floor.success: Advances shared transaction counter monotonically by CAS; does not lower an already higher clock.
clock-floor.failure: No returned error; exhaustion is not guarded by this API.
clock-floor.limitations: No production fail-closed u64 exhaustion protocol is proved or enforced here.

vacuum-pass.preconditions: Live same-arena registration/retention discipline, valid chains and allocator ownership; no concurrent destructive reset.
vacuum-pass.success: Public requested horizon is clamped to observed same-arena retained horizon; reclaims only older unguarded nonheads and returns reclaimed/live-head payload reports. Normal pass computes horizon once and calls internal kernel.
vacuum-pass.failure: Pointer/row/storage errors propagate, possibly after earlier rows were reclaimed; no all-or-nothing vacuum guarantee.
vacuum-pass.limitations: Concurrent horizon/physical pointer/weak-memory assumptions remain explicit; selected source-bound retention proofs cover narrower slices.

horizon.preconditions: Valid same-arena ProcArray and clock, unique registration ownership and no counter wrap.
horizon.success: Returns oldest active retained xmin, or next clock when none, under lifecycle lock.
horizon.failure: No returned error; invalid external metadata manipulation is outside contract.
horizon.limitations: The returned scalar is an observation, not a capability authorizing use on another arena or after arbitrary reset.

vacuum-config.preconditions: Valid callback and interval; callback must obey payload/arena lifetimes.
vacuum-config.success: Builds a daemon configuration; zero interval is normalized when spawning.
vacuum-config.failure: No returned error; allocation/panic remains separate.
vacuum-config.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

vacuum-spawn.preconditions: Valid table and live worker process; no destructive reset; callbacks must not synchronously stop/join their own daemon.
vacuum-spawn.success: Returns leader thread handle or nonleader handle for existing live leader; reclamation callback runs after each pass releases partition guards.
vacuum-spawn.failure: Spawn error may leave this PID in the leader slot; no returned contract promises repair after thread spawn failure. Process liveness/PID reuse and callback panic remain lifecycle risks.
vacuum-spawn.limitations: Thread/process progress and automatic stale-owner recovery are not proved.

vacuum-stop.preconditions: Call from outside the worker thread; retain handle/table until joining.
vacuum-stop.success: Signals and joins owned worker and clears owned leader slot; nonleader handle has no owned worker.
vacuum-stop.failure: Join/worker error returned; poisoned local mutex may panic. Drop attempts stop and ignores its error.
vacuum-stop.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

pk-create.preconditions: Exclusive bootstrap in valid same arena; positive capacity/buckets within representable allocation limits.
pk-create.success: Creates empty PK map or attaches to initialized map using supplied header/bucket offsets.
pk-create.failure: Invalid capacity/metadata, allocation or pointer errors; partial bootstrap allocation can remain.
pk-create.limitations: Attach offset provenance and stable slots are caller obligations.

pk-get.preconditions: Valid map and UTF-8 key representation; entries stay retained.
pk-get.success: Returns existing canonical row ID or None after checking the current bucket chain.
pk-get.failure: Invalid metadata/pointer/key errors; no row read or absence predicate dependency is created.
pk-get.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

pk-insert.preconditions: Valid map/key and stable row namespace; insert_existing supplied row ID is caller-owned and valid.
pk-insert.success: Publishes at most one entry per key; competitors return winning ID after re-search on failed CAS. get_or_insert reserves a physical ID.
pk-insert.failure: Capacity/key/allocation/pointer errors. Losing private entries are recycled; automatic ID reservations can leave holes and exhaust capacity before distinct-key count reaches it.
pk-insert.limitations: Does not seed or transactionally insert an OccTable row; concurrent safe publication is a separate implementation obligation.

executor-new.success: Creates the stateless execution engine value.
executor-new.limitations: Query correctness belongs to execute and snapshot-mode contracts.

query-execute.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Compiled plan uses this schema, stable slots and deterministic nonreentrant row field callbacks.
query-execute.success: Executes index/PK/full-scan route, applies all filters, optional sort and limit using the supplied transaction and its own writes.
query-execute.failure: Planner/Occ errors propagate with accumulated dependencies; caller owns abort/commit.
query-execute.limitations: Return is speculative until caller validates commit. No SQL compatibility or stable tie order is implied.

query-mode.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Valid compiled plan and callbacks.
query-mode.success: StrictSnapshot retries bounded serialization failures and returns only after read-only commit validates. ChunkedEventual scans stable slots in separate snapshots, aborts each registration, then sorts/limits aggregate.
query-mode.failure: Admission/read/cleanup errors propagate; StrictSnapshot exhausts to SerializationFailure. ChunkedEventual can mix times and does not validate a single serial result.
query-mode.limitations: ChunkedEventual is explicitly weaker; it does not commit/validate each chunk as a serializable transaction.

planner-schema.preconditions: Field/index metadata and primary-key namespace match the target table; changes occur outside concurrent execution.
planner-schema.success: Constructs/updates catalog and optimizer metadata or returns access-path/schema fields.
planner-schema.failure: Infallible setters may allocate/panic; no runtime table consistency is established by setting catalog entries.
planner-schema.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

planner-compile.preconditions: Deterministic StapiRow field semantics; schema/index bindings reflect table layout.
planner-compile.success: Parses/compiles driver plus residual predicates, sort and limit; selected access path preserves declared query semantics.
planner-compile.failure: Parse, unknown-field/operator/type/planning errors are explicit PlannerError; no database mutation.
planner-compile.limitations: Rule choice is not an implementation refinement proof; callbacks are an application boundary.

row-callback.preconditions: Caller supplies deterministic pure field extraction and stable schema; no reentry or irreversible effects.
row-callback.success: Reports field presence/value/nullness consistently with stored payload.
row-callback.failure: Option None/false represent absent/null according to method; arbitrary panic/side effects are outside supported callbacks.
row-callback.limitations: Trait does not enforce these semantic requirements.

parser.preconditions: Input text is the intended STAPI/word-list syntax, with normal Rust allocation availability.
parser.success: Produces parsed query/value/word list or formatted parse error; getters observe error/value data.
parser.failure: Malformed query/word-list input returns ParseError where signature allows it. Value::from_atom first parses i64, then f64 only for atoms containing a decimal point or exponent marker; other atoms, including boolean/null-looking words, remain Text. Error/value accessors return their stored or formatted data.
parser.limitations: Parser accepts the implemented STAPI subset; this is not PostgreSQL syntax compatibility.

retry.preconditions: Caller provides resource/scheduling policy and does not sleep while holding publication locks.
retry.success: Computes bounded seeded backoff delays and optionally sleeps for returned duration.
retry.failure: No Result errors; OS scheduling may delay actual wakeup beyond requested duration.
retry.limitations: Not a proof of fairness, bounded transaction latency or eventual success.

proc-begin.preconditions: Valid ProcArray/clock in same live arena; unique ownership and no u64 wrap.
proc-begin.success: Reserves fresh nonzero transaction ID and free slot under lifecycle mutex, publishing retained xmin before use.
proc-begin.failure: No free slot returns ProcArrayError; IDs can be consumed by failed admission.
proc-begin.limitations: Copied public registration values do not mint extra ownership; caller discipline remains required.

proc-end.preconditions: Caller uniquely owns the matching slot/transaction registration.
proc-end.success: Clears matching active slot and horizon under lifecycle mutex.
proc-end.failure: Out-of-range/stale/mismatched registration returns ProcArrayError without clearing another owner.
proc-end.limitations: Registration is Copy; safe API does not enforce unique authority.

proc-snapshot.preconditions: Same-arena live clock/slots, no wrap; transaction form owns a matching live registration.
proc-snapshot.success: Captures active IDs and xmin/xmax coherently under lifecycle lock; transaction form updates owned retained horizon.
proc-snapshot.failure: Plain snapshot/oldest horizon have no returned errors; transaction snapshot rejects invalid/stale registration.
proc-snapshot.limitations: A plain snapshot value alone does not pin storage. Lifetime/interference correctness remains a primitive boundary.

proc-clear.preconditions: Exclusive quiescent attachment/recovery after owner-death policy; no live worker can own discarded slots.
proc-clear.success: Clears all nonzero slots/horizons and returns count under lifecycle mutex.
proc-clear.failure: No returned error; it does not determine which recorded processes are alive.
proc-clear.limitations: Despite its name, clear_orphaned_slots clears all slots; live-worker exclusion is essential and not enforced.

proc-new.preconditions: For new: exclusive creation before publishing ProcArray storage. For snapshot/count accessors: valid receiver under its ordinary lifetime.
proc-new.success: Initializes empty slots/lifecycle state; value getters expose active count/IDs/optional slot ID.
proc-new.failure: No returned error; invalid slot index returns None for slot_txid.
proc-new.limitations: Snapshot view methods do not confer pin ownership.

arena-create.preconditions: Supported Linux mapping and size; exclusive initialization.
arena-create.success: Creates anonymous shared mapping and valid initialized arena header.
arena-create.failure: InvalidSize/MmapFailed/initialization errors are returned; failed mapping construction releases owned mapping when supported.
arena-create.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

arena-reset.preconditions: Exclusive owner after all old handles, references, registrations and workers are gone.
arena-reset.failure: Invalid size or header setup errors; operation is destructive and not rolled back.
arena-reset.limitations: Safe public signature does not enforce exclusivity; never treat this as ordinary attachment.

arena-admin.preconditions: Exclusive lifecycle authority or unique daemon owner appropriate to field; same live arena.
arena-admin.success: Sets clean-shutdown/layout/daemon metadata or atomically compares daemon PID; no logical transaction commit.
arena-admin.failure: Setters have no Result; CAS returns observed competing PID; no process liveness or layout validation is implied.
arena-admin.limitations: Public mutable metadata/clock access can violate higher-level contracts; capability enforcement remains open.

arena-alloc.preconditions: Valid arena, representable nonzero size/alignment and requested class; typed payload valid for shared storage.
arena-alloc.success: Removes one fitting recycled block or advances arena allocation, then initializes typed payload for alloc variants.
arena-alloc.failure: Invalid layout/size, arena full/offset exhaustion and storage errors returned; no arbitrary allocation-success guarantee.
arena-alloc.limitations: Cross-process payload representation, type/lifetime/provenance and allocation ownership remain assumptions/open proofs.

arena-recycle.preconditions: Caller exclusively owns exactly this allocated block of matching class/size/alignment; it is detached and unpinned; recycle once.
arena-recycle.success: Adds reusable in-band block to matching shared class free list; too-small blocks are intentionally not put on that list.
arena-recycle.failure: Layout/bounds/storage errors; no caller ownership check. Compatibility flush is a no-op because lists are already shared.
arena-recycle.limitations: Safe public signature does not prevent double recycling or recycling a live block.

relptr.preconditions: Offset denotes appropriately aligned, initialized, valid T in the exact live mapping, with ownership/pin lasting for returned reference. Atomic orderings must be legal for chosen operation.
relptr.success: Constructs/loads/stores/exchanges offset; as_ref returns typed reference when nonnull range/alignment checks pass, None otherwise.
relptr.failure: CAS returns competing offset; illegal atomic order can panic. Bounds checks cannot turn arbitrary bytes into valid T.
relptr.limitations: Safe as_ref accepts caller-fabricated offsets; this is an open soundness/API enforcement issue, not a proved safe abstraction.

partition-raw-lock.preconditions: Correct shared lock instance, ownership discipline and pairing; only crate-visible users can name the unexported lock module.
partition-raw-lock.success: try_lock claims an unlocked lock; unlock releases it.
partition-raw-lock.failure: try_lock false means contention; no returned ownership validation.
partition-raw-lock.limitations: Raw unlock can be misused; owned guard/CAS contracts, weak memory and process death remain boundaries.

boot.preconditions: Exclusive bootstrap/recovery or externally guaranteed quiescent valid warm attachment; stable file identity/layout/size; no live worker during reset/slot clearing.
boot.success: Calls map_tmpfs_shared, selects ColdReplay or WarmAttach after loading the stored BootLayout, resets invalid/missing warm layout to cold replay, clears all ProcArray slots only on the required quiescent warm path, marks running and returns BootContext.
boot.failure: Mapping/header reset errors propagate. Invalid warm layout is intentionally converted into destructive cold reset/replay instead of returned; earlier initialization/admin effects need not roll back.
boot.limitations: open_boot_context is not ordinary concurrent worker attachment: it lacks enforced interprocess startup authority and its warm path clears all recorded slots. Workers must not be live during this startup action.

index-create.preconditions: Valid shared arena and pure stable key representation; exclusive first creation or valid existing offsets.
index-create.success: Creates/attaches index header and shared skiplist.
index-create.failure: Fallible attachment returns pointer/format errors; new/new_in_shared panic on construction failure because they use expect.
index-create.limitations: Current-posting raw index is not a snapshot database query.

index-mutate.preconditions: Unbound index under raw mutation management lock; canonical key and serializable row ID; bound indexes mutate only through internal transaction driver.
index-mutate.success: Inserts/removes/moves payload under one structural guard; move prepares destination before source removal.
index-mutate.failure: try variants return encoding/allocation/storage or bound-owner rejection. Convenience insert/remove discard errors; they must not be used where silent failure is acceptable only as success.
index-mutate.limitations: No table-row atomicity is supplied for external raw mutation. Generic serialization/callback behavior remains a boundary.

index-read-raw.preconditions: Valid index; use for diagnostics/bootstrap or under caller-held transactional predicate guards when invoked internally.
index-read-raw.success: Enumerates/counts current postings or entries, respecting optional limit and predicate.
index-read-raw.failure: try variants return key/codec/epoch/storage errors; convenience lookup/count/traverse suppress errors or partial traversal as implemented.
index-read-raw.limitations: No transaction dependency, old snapshot candidate guarantee or linearizable multi-call snapshot; explicitly excluded from serial query contract.

index-audit.preconditions: Valid index, structural exclusion/ownership invariants and stable metadata.
index-audit.success: Reports structural allocation census/telemetry; inconsistent census returns error.
index-audit.failure: Audit errors expose malformed or duplicate ownership; diagnostic counters can be approximate under concurrency.
index-audit.limitations: Not a repair operation or proof of complete arena conservation.

index-gc.preconditions: Live same-arena epoch registrations, detached-node ownership and collector daemon policy.
index-gc.success: Reclaims eligible retired storage under priority mutation lock and collector guard; reports count or starts/stops/joins GC daemon.
index-gc.failure: Count forms may return zero on invalid metadata/contention/no work; daemon APIs return spawn/signal/wait failures. Forced termination can abandon a shared mutex, requiring recovery.
index-gc.limitations: Fairness, process death, memory bound and physical safe reuse remain separate obligations.

skip-create.preconditions: Exclusive construction or live initialized header offset for same typed list/arena; valid sentinel and representation.
skip-create.success: Allocates shared header/sentinel storage or attaches after format/pointer validation.
skip-create.failure: Allocation, pointer, format and epoch/structural initialization errors returned; partial bootstrap allocation may remain.
skip-create.limitations: Attachment checks do not establish pointer provenance, payload type or unique ownership.

skip-mutate.preconditions: Valid initialized typed skiplist; pure total stable key comparison; exclusive structural guard acquired by API; payload ownership and size valid.
skip-mutate.success: Inserts/removes/moves payload with epoch pin under mutation lock, preserving current logical postings.
skip-mutate.failure: Key/storage/allocation/epoch errors returned; move destination allocation precedes source mutation. Arbitrary corruption can expose partial cleanup.
skip-mutate.limitations: Visitors/comparators cannot reenter this list or invert outer table/index lock order; raw pointer/allocator semantics remain open.

skip-read.preconditions: Valid list with pure stable keys; visitors are nonreentrant and cannot acquire outer locks.
skip-read.success: Looks up/scans/counts under mutation lock and temporary epoch registration, invoking visitor for selected payloads.
skip-read.failure: Pointer/key/epoch/storage errors returned; visitor may already have observed a prefix before failure.
skip-read.limitations: Callback panic releases Rust RAII guards but arbitrary side effects/owner death are outside Result contract.

skip-key.preconditions: Pure deterministic total order, valid sentinel strictly compatible with stored keys, no mutation/reentry in comparison.
skip-key.success: Supplies sentinel/order used by shared list.
skip-key.failure: No Result errors; arbitrary callback panic or inconsistent order violates the supported key contract.
skip-key.limitations: Trait signatures do not enforce order laws or process-independent representation.

index-value.preconditions: Deterministic value conversion compatible with canonical index key representation.
index-value.failure: No Result errors; caller conversion may panic if custom implementation does so.
index-value.limitations: Custom trait behavior must meet schema/key contract; not automatically verified.

committer-create.preconditions: Synchronous path or same-arena live async ring; one stream per table once first bound.
committer-create.success: Constructs selected committer, reports mode/path, or validates proposed stream without mutation.
committer-create.failure: I/O opening errors, missing async ring/invalid mode, wrong arena or stream mismatch are explicit.
committer-create.limitations: Validation does not bind; first commit attempt can bind even if that attempt later fails.

wal-commit.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Matching single WAL stream, deterministic correct codec/baselines, live daemon for async progress; no concurrent reset.
wal-commit.success: Accepts complete WAL before row publication: sync includes fdatasync, async only ring enqueue. Then publishes and returns final-write count; updates async baseline cache after guard release.
wal-commit.failure: Preparation/clean acceptance failure aborts unpublished transaction; stale epoch yields serialization retry. Indeterminate append rollback or PublicationAfterWal poisons table and requires recovery, never blind retry.
wal-commit.limitations: Sync survival assumes OS/filesystem semantics; async may lose dependency-closed suffix. Full volatile/recovery composition remains open.

sync-wal-raw.preconditions: Caller enforces stream framing/order and stop/recovery discipline; no table health boundary on raw append_commit.
sync-wal-raw.success: Opens file or appends and fdatasyncs complete framed record under per-open-description flock; child reopens inherited writer after fork.
sync-wal-raw.failure: I/O/codec errors; failed append attempts truncation/sync rollback, indeterminate tail failure remains explicit.
sync-wal-raw.limitations: Raw use is outside managed table commit correctness; owner death mid-frame requires recovery.

wal-daemon.preconditions: One live daemon per ring, valid file identity, supported fork/process lifecycle; prior owner joined before restart.
wal-daemon.success: Spawns consumer to append complete frames, or observes/signals/waits for child status.
wal-daemon.failure: I/O/spawn/invalid owner/file errors and unexpected exit status propagate; join_any_status returns raw status.
wal-daemon.limitations: Killing daemon, PID reuse, lost shared locks and reset authority require lifecycle discipline; not general robust owner-death recovery.

checkpoint.preconditions: Valid, live, identically typed arena/table; complete bound indexes with identical deterministic extractors; preseeded stable row slots; no concurrent bootstrap/reset; counters do not wrap. A transaction belongs to this table/mapping and remains registered until completion. Speculative observations cause no irreversible effects. Matching synchronous file stream or unbound bootstrap table; exclusive checkpoint path use; no async stream.
checkpoint.success: Holds all partitions across row/snapshot capture, durable temp-file rename+parent sync and WAL truncation; records active IDs and cutoff. Returns row count.
checkpoint.failure: Stream mismatch rejects async/wrong file; I/O/codec/storage error may leave published checkpoint or partial admin work. Never infer whole administrative operation rollback.
checkpoint.limitations: Consistent-cut target and regression evidence do not prove all filesystem crash schedules.

replay.preconditions: Exclusive cold recovery into correct unbound table/schema; immutable complete checkpoint/WAL inputs and consistent delta baseline/PK map.
replay.success: Applies supported checkpoint and complete WAL transactions in recorded order, restores row IDs/txid floor, returns recovery state/count.
replay.failure: Codec, missing base, bounds, I/O, unsupported version or corrupt/truncated record errors. Earlier replayed prefix may remain; do not serve partially recovered arena.
replay.limitations: Rebuild indexes after rows under exclusive bootstrap. Does not clear/reset arbitrary live table or provide rollback-on-error.

read-wal.preconditions: Stable input file under exclusive recovery or external append/read coordination.
read-wal.success: Reads framed records in file order and decodes complete contents; a missing file returns an empty record list.
read-wal.failure: I/O, invalid frame length, incomplete payload or decode error is explicit; this API does not promise arbitrary corrupt-tail salvage.
read-wal.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

wal-encode.preconditions: Correct codec, dirty mask, before/after values and base-version correspondence; allocation available.
wal-encode.success: Builds complete commit/update record, serializes it, decodes it or applies selected delta to matching baseline.
wal-encode.failure: Codec/length/schema/baseline errors returned where signature permits; custom codec can partially mutate supplied value/output before error.
wal-encode.limitations: Does not itself persist, order or publish a database transaction; codec round-trip laws remain a contract.

delta-bytes.preconditions: Byte arrays use selected 64-bit mask/chunk convention; matching unchanged base length for overlays.
delta-bytes.success: Computes conservative changed chunks, packs selected bytes, or overlays validated payload into base.
delta-bytes.failure: apply_delta_bytes returns invalid-length errors; pure mask/pack functions return values directly.
delta-bytes.limitations: Bitmask is not schema-independent: caller must choose correct codec and baseline.

copy-mask.preconditions: Both values have all bytes initialized and readable, including padding, with stable object representation.
copy-mask.success: Compares raw Copy representation to compute coarse dirty mask.
copy-mask.failure: No Result failure path. Violating initialized-padding premise is a potential Rust soundness defect, not an ordinary error.
copy-mask.limitations: Copy alone does not establish this premise; native write calls this helper. Replace with explicit representation/fieldwise encoding in later implementation work.

ring-create.preconditions: Exclusive creation or valid same-arena live initialized ring pointer; const capacity/slot size valid.
ring-create.success: Initializes empty ring or attaches handle; accessors report ring pointer/state/epoch.
ring-create.failure: Shared creation may allocate/fail; from_existing defers pointer validation to operations.
ring-create.limitations: Raw slots/header authority and generic capacity arithmetic are not proved.

ring-push.preconditions: Single valid ring protocol with live consumer for progress; payload fits slot; no destructive reset.
ring-push.success: Reserves and publishes one complete payload; commit wrapper serializes first. Blocking push waits while full.
ring-push.failure: Closed/oversize/invalid storage/codec errors reject. No bounded wait or durable acknowledgement is promised.
ring-push.limitations: Managed commit may hold predicate/partition locks while enqueue waits; daemon must drain without those locks.

ring-pop.preconditions: Valid live ring and correct consumer discipline; destination buffer large enough by type.
ring-pop.success: Consumes at most one complete payload; None means no available record.
ring-pop.failure: Invalid storage/closed/codec errors propagate for fallible wrappers; no transaction replay is performed.
ring-pop.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

ring-reset.preconditions: Exclusive stopped/joined producer-consumer lifecycle before destructive restart; never reset live ring.
ring-reset.success: Clears queued slot state, head/tail, closed flag and writer-claimed flag for exclusive restart; it does not itself bump the writer epoch.
ring-reset.failure: Direct reset has no Result; the SharedWalRing wrapper can return invalid-pointer error.
ring-reset.limitations: Safe public methods do not enforce owner exclusivity or a no-wrap epoch policy.

mode-setting.preconditions: Text configuration interpreted by current implementation.
mode-setting.success: Recognized off-like settings select asynchronous mode; other settings choose synchronous mode.
mode-setting.failure: No parse error is returned; caller must validate unknown settings if required.
mode-setting.limitations: Implementation correctness remains subject to the claim and assumption ledgers; defining this contract is not a proof.

ring-close.preconditions: Valid live ring and authority to request admission shutdown. Concurrent producers must be stopped/joined separately before claiming a fully drained durable shutdown.
ring-close.success: Release-stores the closed flag. Producers observing it return Closed; a producer that already passed its check may still publish. Existing contents are not erased.
ring-close.failure: Direct close has no returned error; SharedWalRing wrapper can return invalid-pointer error.
ring-close.limitations: Close is allowed during live operation, unlike destructive reset. It neither cancels in-flight pushes nor drains/fsyncs the ring.

ring-epoch.preconditions: Valid live ring; authorized writer-generation change under lifecycle discipline; no u64 epoch wrap.
ring-epoch.success: Atomically increments writer epoch and returns the new value so managed commit preparation detects changed baseline generation.
ring-epoch.failure: Direct method has no Result; wrapper can return invalid-pointer error. Overflow wraps in current implementation.
ring-epoch.limitations: The atomic increment does not reset/drain the ring or establish exclusive writer ownership. Writer admission and prior-owner joining are separate operations.

boot-layout-new.preconditions: No shared-storage access; caller supplies row_capacity representable as u32.
boot-layout-new.success: Constructs a versioned BootLayout value with given capacity and zero offsets/counts. Zero capacity is representable here but is rejected by later layout validation.
boot-layout-new.failure: LayoutCorrupt when capacity does not fit u32.
boot-layout-new.limitations: Does not allocate/map arena storage, seed rows, validate referenced offsets or persist layout.

boot-layout-persist.preconditions: Exclusive bootstrap/recovery authority, valid live arena and initialized aligned BootLayout storage at any existing layout offset. Supplied layout has valid magic/version, positive capacity and bounded index count.
boot-layout-persist.success: Allocates and publishes a first layout offset or overwrites the existing layout in place; returns that offset.
boot-layout-persist.failure: LayoutCorrupt or allocation errors; no transactional rollback of bootstrap storage is promised.
boot-layout-persist.limitations: Validation checks layout fields, not provenance/liveness of all referenced rows, index arrays or ring. Existing-layout rewrite requires exclusion from readers.

boot-layout-load.preconditions: Valid live arena; any nonzero layout offset names an initialized aligned BootLayout retained for the read.
boot-layout-load.success: Returns None for zero offset; otherwise copies the layout after magic/version/capacity/index-count validation.
boot-layout-load.failure: LayoutCorrupt for failed pointer/header checks or invalid fields.
boot-layout-load.limitations: No recursive verification of referenced table/index/ring storage and no ownership capability is produced.

boot-array-allocate.preconditions: Valid arena and exclusive ownership of newly allocated storage; input length fits returned u32 length and available representable arena space.
boot-array-allocate.success: Returns (0,0) for empty input; otherwise allocates aligned u32 storage, copies elements and returns (offset,length).
boot-array-allocate.failure: LayoutCorrupt for checked size/address overflow or allocation error; earlier allocation can remain on a later bootstrap error.
boot-array-allocate.limitations: Does not publish a BootLayout or validate offsets stored as array elements; caller controls their later interpretation.

boot-array-read.preconditions: For nonzero offset/length, caller supplies an aligned, initialized, live u32 array in this exact arena; no concurrent mutation during copying.
boot-array-read.success: Returns empty vector when either offset or length is zero; otherwise copies length elements from the bounded range.
boot-array-read.failure: LayoutCorrupt for checked size/range overflow or range beyond arena; ordinary Rust allocation panic/abort remains separate.
boot-array-read.limitations: Native check covers range, not u32 alignment, initialization, provenance or pinning. Safe signature does not enforce those preconditions.

boot-layout-clear.preconditions: Exclusive lifecycle authority; all users of the previous published layout are quiescent.
boot-layout-clear.success: Sets published boot-layout offset to zero.
boot-layout-clear.limitations: Does not reclaim the prior allocation, reset the arena or stop live workers.

arena-map.preconditions: Supported Linux file mapping with stable file identity; exclusive authority for creation, size change or header reset. A warm mapping must already have valid matching size/layout and retained ownership.
arena-map.success: Maps shared file, initializes invalid/new header as ColdStart or reports valid existing header as WarmStart, and clears clean-shutdown flag.
arena-map.failure: I/O, invalid-size, mmap or header initialization errors returned. The existing file may already have been resized on failure.
arena-map.limitations: Existing size mismatch causes ftruncate; no interprocess startup lock enforces authority. This method does not load BootLayout or clear ProcArray slots.

lock_nodes.stable_rows: Optional caller-owned stable-slot IndexedUpdateGuard; acquire sorted/deduplicated row IDs all at once before begin.
lock_nodes.registry: OccSharedHeader.index_registry_lock; registration, sealing and first WAL-stream binding.
lock_nodes.predicate: Per-index predicate bucket mutexes; globally sorted by shared index header then bucket.
lock_nodes.partitions: Shared OCC row-partition lock set; sorted/deduplicated ascending partition IDs, reverse release.
lock_nodes.management: SecondaryIndex management_lock; raw mutation versus binding ownership.
lock_nodes.mutation: One skiplist structural mutation lock; nonreentrant, priority acquisition for collection.
lock_nodes.collector: Skiplist gc_collect_lock, single nonblocking CAS guard under mutation lock.
lock_nodes.lifecycle: ProcArray lifecycle mutex; scope-local, never retained with the snapshot value or registration.
lock_nodes.row_recycle: One table row-recycle shard mutex at a time; not the partition lock.
lock_nodes.arena_class: One shared allocator free-list class mutex at a time.
lock_nodes.wal_file: OS flock on independently opened WAL file description; file must outlive guard.
lock_nodes.ring_capacity: Bounded async ring enqueue space; waiting resource, not a table lock.
lock_nodes.row_owner: Longer-lived OccRow ownership flag held by RowLockGuard, distinct from partition mutex.
lock_nodes.vacuum_handle: Process-local VacuumDaemon thread-handle mutex; guard drops after take() statement.
lock_nodes.worker_join: Joining owned vacuum worker after releasing local handle mutex.
lock_nodes.callback: Application extractor/visitor/codec/reclaim callback; restrictions differ by call site.

lock_edges.reason: Caller acquires all stable row guards before begin or commit; nested additional stable-row acquisition is forbidden.
Optional caller guard may remain through transaction lookup/commit, which acquire their own predicate sets.
Caller guard can enclose row locking or commit; engine does not acquire stable guards inside these operations.
Binding initial index snapshots and binding the first WAL stream acquire all partitions under registry.
First binding enumerates actual postings while registry is held; snapshot row-partition guard has already returned.
Binding shared index owner takes management mutex under table registry, after initial census scopes finish.
begin releases registry scope before shm.begin_transaction; registration is not a held mutex.
Commit acquires complete predicate set first, then bounded row-partition set; partition failure releases predicates before abort backoff.
Indexed lookup captures current postings under predicate guards, taking structural lookup guard and epoch pin.
